# Results — Study 213 (Meme Stocks) on the real tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Basket: GME, AMC,
BB, BBBY, KOSS, NOK — equal-weight — vs SPY (S&P 500, total-return
auto-adjusted). Two entry scenarios and one momentum-timed variant. Costs: **20
bps** one-way. As-of **2026-06-15**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold
the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Meme basket (6 tickers) + SPY benchmark | 2020-01-02 → 2026-06-15 | 6 tickers × 1,621 days | `7a41c83110bf` |

## Survivorship and delisting disclosure (no silent caps)

- **BBBY (Bed Bath & Beyond)** filed for bankruptcy and was delisted
  **2023-04-26**. It is kept in the basket through its full live period; its
  loss is absorbed by the backtest — no silent removal.
- **AMC, BB, NOK** remain listed but have lost 42–92% of their January-2021
  value. The basket's positive headline (Strategy A) is carried almost entirely
  by **GME**, a single name.
- The momentum-timed strategy fires triggers in **August–September 2020** —
  before the WSB mania went viral in late January 2021. Those signals are not
  ex-ante replicable as a *meme strategy*; they are accidental pre-mania
  momentum in small-caps.

## Strategy A — Buy-and-Hold from 2021-01-04 (first trading day of the mania year)

Equal-weight entry at the close on 2021-01-04; held to 2025-12-31.

| Arm | Total return | CAGR | Sharpe | Annualised vol | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Meme basket (equal-weight)** | **+186.6%** | **23.5%/yr** | **0.57** | **100.7%/yr** | **−84.2%** |
| SPY (S&P 500) | +98.1% | 14.7%/yr | 0.89 | 17.1%/yr | −24.5% |

Individual ticker returns (2021-01-04 → 2025-12-31):

| Ticker | Return |
|---|--:|
| GME | +366% |
| NOK | +85% |
| KOSS | +30% |
| BB | −42% |
| BBBY | −89% |
| AMC | −92% |

The basket's positive headline is a statistical accident: **one name (GME)
posted +366%** while four of six names lost more than 40%. Equal-weighting
a basket of four losers and two survivors is not an investable result — it is
an illustration of the **left-tail skewness** of meme stocks.

## Strategy B — Buy at peak / "retail entered the news" scenario

Entry on 2021-01-28 (the day after the WSB squeeze was front-page news;
the moment most retail interest peaked):

| Arm | Total return | CAGR | Sharpe | Vol | Max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Meme basket** | **−45.0%** | **−11.4%/yr** | **0.11** | **63.4%/yr** | **−84.2%** |
| SPY | +93.4% | +14.3%/yr | 0.87 | 17.1%/yr | −24.5% |

This is the exit-liquidity scenario: **−45% total return vs +93% for SPY**
over the same ~5 years. Entering at peak costs −139 percentage points of
total return relative to SPY.

## Strategy C — Momentum-timed (60-day look-back, +50% threshold, 126-day hold)

Signals that fired and their results:

| Ticker | Entry | Exit | Net return |
|---|---|---|--:|
| BBBY | 2020-08-26 | 2021-02-26 | −39.1% |
| KOSS | 2020-08-26 | 2021-02-26 | +680.4% |
| GME | 2020-09-01 | 2021-03-04 | +1,629.7% |
| BB | 2020-12-03 | 2021-06-07 | +111.0% |
| AMC | 2021-01-26 | 2021-07-27 | +665.9% |
| NOK | 2021-01-28 | 2021-07-29 | +28.6% |

Mean net return: **+512.8%** across 6 trades. Win rate: **83%**.
HAC *t* = **2.18** on n = 6 (WARNING: n=6 has no inference power; the t-stat
is meaningless at this sample size).

The dominant trades (GME +1630%, KOSS +680%) entered in **August–September
2020**, months before the WSB mania became public knowledge. A practitioner
running this strategy in real time would not have identified GME as a
*meme stock* on 2020-09-01 — that label only crystallised in January 2021. The
apparent momentum edge is therefore **look-ahead-contaminated by basket
construction**: we selected the basket from names that *became* memes in
hindsight, then found momentum signals that preceded the mania.

## Verdict summary

| Dimension | Finding |
|---|---|
| **Signal** | **None** — the Strategy A headline is driven by one name out of six; Strategy B (realistic retail timing) loses 45% vs +93% for SPY; the momentum signal is n=6 and look-ahead-tainted. No certifiable edge at any entry point a real investor could have used. |
| **Tradability** | **Mirage** — 100%+/yr vol, −84% max drawdown, single-name concentration, one delisting. The "edge" in Strategy A requires having bought all six names on a single equal-weight ticket before the mania and held through a −84% peak drawdown. |
| **Myth check** | The meme-stock mania was real — but the money went to a small number of pre-mania holders, short-sellers who covered at the top, and options market makers. The retail crowd that bought the news (Strategy B) lost −45% while the S&P 500 doubled. |
